about: House recipes, batch 02 (8 October 2026): 100 more recipes written for v2, mostly dinners with breakfasts, lunches and snacks, across all 25 cuisines. All are ai-draft until Lachlan reviews or cook-tests them (D-044).

recipes.title: Chicken Saltimbocca
recipes.summary: Thin chicken escalopes wrapped in prosciutto and sage, pan-fried and finished with a buttery white wine sauce.
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thin fillets, then cut each in half again so you have 8 pieces. Lay them between two sheets of baking paper and flatten with a rolling pin to about 1cm thick.

Season the chicken lightly with salt and pepper (go easy on salt, as the prosciutto is salty). Lay a sage leaf on each piece and wrap a slice of prosciutto around it, pressing so it sticks. Dust both sides with flour and shake off the excess.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken prosciutto-side down first for 3 minutes, until crisp, then turn and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Cook in two batches if needed and keep warm on a plate.

Pour the wine into the pan and let it bubble for 1 minute, scraping up the browned bits. Add the stock and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until reduced by half. Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the butter a few pieces at a time until glossy, then add the lemon juice.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan to coat. Serve with the sauce spooned over, rocket and lemon wedges.
notes: Veal escalopes are the classic version and cook in about the same time; veal can be served slightly pink.
Mashed potato or crusty bread is good for the sauce.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Puttanesca
recipes.summary: A punchy pantry pasta of tomatoes, olives, capers, anchovies and chilli, on the table in 25 minutes.

items: 1 tsp salt, plus more for the pasta water
Small handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

steps: Bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to the boil.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic, anchovies and chilli flakes and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the anchovies melt into the oil and the garlic is pale gold.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers and oregano. Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Taste and add salt only if needed.
Cook the spaghetti until just al dente, about 1 minute less than the packet says. Scoop out a cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the spaghetti into the sauce with a splash of the pasta water and cook for 1 minute, until the sauce clings. Scatter with parsley and serve.
notes: The anchovies dissolve and give depth rather than fishiness. For a vegetarian version leave them out and add another tablespoon of capers.

image.credit: Photo: Popo le Chien / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Zucchini and Herb Frittata
recipes.summary: A thick, soft-set frittata of golden zucchini, parmesan, mint and basil, good warm or cold.
steps: Toss the grated zucchini with half the salt in a colander and leave for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much water as you can with your hands.

Heat the oven grill to medium-high. Warm the oil in a 24cm ovenproof non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Cook the spring onion for 2 minutes, then add the zucchini and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, until dry and starting to colour.
Whisk the eggs with the parmesan, the rest of the salt, pepper and most of the herbs.
Add the butter to the pan, let it melt, then pour in the eggs. Cook over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes without stirring, until the edges are set and the top is still a little wet.
Slide the pan under the grill for 3 to 4 minutes, until the top is set and lightly golden. Rest for 5 minutes, then slide onto a board, scatter with the rest of the herbs and cut into wedges.
notes: Keeps covered in the fridge for 2 days and makes a good lunchbox slice.

recipes.title: Panzanella
recipes.summary: Tuscan bread salad of ripe tomatoes, cucumber and toasted sourdough soaking up a sharp red wine vinegar dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced). Toss the bread with the oil on a tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp outside but still a little chewy in the middle.
Put the tomatoes in a large bowl with the salt and leave for 10 minutes to release their juices.
Whisk the dressing ingredients together and pour over the tomatoes. Add the cucumber, onion, capers and toasted bread and toss well.
Leave for 10 to 15 minutes so the bread soaks up the juices, then tear in the basil, toss again and serve.
notes: It needs properly ripe, summer tomatoes. Out of season, use cherry tomatoes, halved.

image.credit: Photo: Heather Katsoulis / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Steak au Poivre
recipes.summary: Pepper-crusted sirloin seared hard and served with a brandy and cream pan sauce and crisp oven chips.
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Heat the oven and cook the chips according to the packet.
Crush the peppercorns coarsely in a mortar and pestle or under a heavy pan. Pat the steaks dry, season with salt and press the pepper firmly onto both sides.

Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan over high heat until shimmering. Cook the steaks for 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium-rare, adding the butter for the last minute and spooning it over. Rest on a warm plate for 5 minutes.

Pour off most of the fat and turn the heat to medium. Cook the shallot for 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat, add the brandy, then return it and let it bubble for 30 seconds (stand back, as it can flare). Add the stock and boil for 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in the cream and any resting juices and simmer for 2 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon. Serve the steaks with the sauce poured over, chips and salad.
notes: Never add brandy to a pan over a gas flame straight from the bottle; pour it into a cup first.
Check the label on your frozen chips if gluten matters: some are coated in wheat flour.

image.credit: Photo: Mark Mitchell / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

recipes.title: Moules Marinières
recipes.summary: Mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic and shallots, with a splash of cream and bread for the broth.

items: Large handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

steps: Rinse the mussels in cold water and pull off the hairy beards. Tap any open mussels on the bench: throw away any that don't close, and any with cracked shells.
Melt the butter in a large, wide saucepan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the shallots, garlic, thyme and bay leaf for 3 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Turn the heat to high, add the wine and bring to a rolling boil. Tip in the mussels, cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan once or twice, until the shells have opened.
Lift the mussels into warm bowls with a slotted spoon, discarding any that stay shut. Stir the cream, parsley and pepper into the broth and bring back to the boil.
Pour the broth over the mussels and serve straight away with bread for dipping and a bowl for the shells.
notes: Buy mussels on the day you cook them and keep them in the fridge in an open bag under a damp cloth, not in water.
Leave out the cream for a lighter, dairy-free broth (use olive oil instead of butter).

recipes.title: Leek and Potato Soup
recipes.summary: A silky, gently buttery French soup of slow-softened leeks and potatoes, finished with cream and chives.

items: 3 leeks (white and pale green parts), sliced and washed

steps: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the leeks, onion and garlic with a pinch of the salt, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft but not browned.
Add the potatoes, stock, bay leaf and thyme. Bring to the boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.
Fish out the bay leaf and thyme stalks. Blend until smooth with a stick blender (or in batches in a blender, with the lid vented).
Stir in the cream, the rest of the salt and the white pepper and warm through without boiling. Serve scattered with chives, with bread on the side.
notes: Leeks hide grit between their layers: slice them first, then swish in a big bowl of water and lift them out.
Chill it and serve cold in summer and it becomes vichyssoise.

recipes.title: Crêpes with Lemon and Sugar
recipes.summary: Thin, lacy French pancakes rolled with a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of caster sugar.

items: 30g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl. Make a well, add the eggs and a splash of the milk and whisk to a thick, smooth paste. Gradually whisk in the rest of the milk, then the melted butter. The batter should be the consistency of pouring cream.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes at room temperature (or up to a day in the fridge).
Heat a 22 to 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little butter. Pour in about 3 tbsp of batter and swirl quickly to coat the base thinly.

Cook for about 1 minute, until the edges lift and the underside is golden, then flip and cook for 30 seconds more. Stack the crêpes on a plate under a tea towel while you cook the rest. The first one is usually a tester.
To serve, squeeze lemon over each crêpe, sprinkle with sugar, and fold into quarters or roll up.
notes: Makes about 12. Leftover crêpes keep in the fridge, layered with baking paper, for 2 days.

recipes.title: Patatas Bravas
recipes.summary: Crisp oven-roasted potatoes with a smoky, spicy tomato sauce and a drizzle of garlicky aioli.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan-forced). Put the potatoes in a saucepan of cold salted water, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain well and leave to steam dry for 5 minutes, then shake in the pan to rough up the edges.
Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt on a large tray in a single layer. Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, make the sauce: warm the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, smoked paprika and cayenne and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the passata, vinegar, sugar and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Blend smooth if you like.
Pile the potatoes on a plate, spoon over the bravas sauce, drizzle with aioli and scatter with parsley. Serve hot.
notes: Shop-bought aioli is fine here. Homemade aioli is made with raw egg, which isn't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system.
Halve the cayenne for a milder sauce.

image.credit: Photo: Kent Wang / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Gambas al Ajillo
recipes.summary: Prawns sizzled in plenty of garlicky, chilli-spiked olive oil, with bread to mop up every drop.

items: 600g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined, tails on
1 small dried chilli, crumbled (or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes)

steps: Pat the prawns dry with paper towel and season with the salt.

Put the oil, garlic and chilli in a wide frying pan or shallow flameproof dish over medium-low heat. Cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and just turning pale gold. Don't let it brown or it turns bitter.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the prawns in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes a side, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Sprinkle over the paprika and add the sherry, if using, and let it sizzle for 30 seconds. Scatter with parsley.
Serve straight from the pan, still sizzling, with lemon wedges and bread for the oil.
notes: The prawns overcook quickly: take them off the heat as soon as they curl and turn opaque.

recipes.title: Pan con Tomate
recipes.summary: Catalan toast rubbed with garlic, topped with grated ripe tomato, good olive oil and flaky salt.
steps: Halve the tomatoes crossways and grate the cut sides on the coarse side of a box grater into a bowl, until only the skin is left in your hand. Throw away the skins and stir a pinch of the salt into the pulp.
Toast or chargrill the bread until golden and crisp on both sides.
While it's hot, rub one side of each slice lightly with the cut garlic.
Spoon the tomato over the toast, drizzle generously with olive oil and finish with flaky salt. Top with jamón if you like, and eat straight away.
notes: Without the jamón it's vegan.

recipes.title: Albóndigas in Tomato Sauce
recipes.summary: Tender Spanish pork and beef meatballs simmered in a smoky paprika and white wine tomato sauce.
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. Add the beef, pork, egg, garlic, parsley, paprika, salt and pepper and mix with your hands until just combined. With wet hands, roll into walnut-sized balls (about 24).

Heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in two batches for 5 minutes, turning, until coloured all over. They don't need to be cooked through yet. Set aside.
Turn the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pan for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.

Add the tomatoes, stock, bay leaf and salt and bring to a simmer. Return the meatballs, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the sauce has thickened and the meatballs are cooked through (75°C in the centre).
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread for the sauce.
notes: Serve as tapas with toothpicks, or with rice or chips as a main.

image.credit: Photo: Juan Emilio Prades Bel / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Spanakopita
recipes.summary: Crisp layers of buttery filo around a creamy spinach, feta, dill and spring onion filling.

items: 500g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan-forced) and brush a 20 x 30cm baking dish with butter.
Warm the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the spring onions for 3 minutes until soft. Cool for a few minutes.
In a bowl, mix the spinach, spring onions, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, mint, nutmeg and pepper. The feta is salty, so there's no need to add salt.
Keep the filo under a damp tea towel while you work. Lay one sheet in the dish, letting it come up the sides, and brush with butter. Repeat with 5 more sheets. Spread the filling over evenly.

Fold the overhanging filo in over the filling. Layer the remaining 6 sheets on top, brushing each with butter, and tuck the edges in. Score the top into 12 pieces with a sharp knife, without cutting through to the filling, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp and the filling is set. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
notes: Squeeze the spinach really dry in a clean tea towel, or the base goes soggy.
Use 1kg of fresh English spinach, wilted and squeezed, instead of the frozen.

image.credit: Photo: Tanya Bakogiannis / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

recipes.title: Pastitsio
recipes.summary: Greek baked pasta with a cinnamon-spiced beef sauce under a thick, golden layer of béchamel.
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, then the mince, and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, oregano, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and not watery. Remove the bay leaf.
Meanwhile, cook the penne in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain, then toss with the egg white and parmesan (this helps the pasta layer hold together).

For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and keep whisking for 6 to 8 minutes until thick and smooth. Take it off the heat, stir in the nutmeg and salt and cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg yolks and half the parmesan.

Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced). Spread half the pasta in a 23 x 33cm baking dish, top with all the meat sauce, then the rest of the pasta. Pour over the béchamel, smooth it and scatter with the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden on top and bubbling. Rest for at least 20 minutes before cutting, so it holds its shape.
notes: Traditionally made with long, hollow pastitsio pasta or bucatini. Penne is easier to find and works well.
Lamb mince is also good here, or half beef, half lamb.

image.credit: Photo: Robert Kindermann / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.5)

recipes.title: Avgolemono
recipes.summary: Greek chicken and rice soup turned silky and bright with a whisked egg and lemon finish.
steps: Put the stock, chicken, onion and bay leaf in a large saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Lift out the chicken, onion and bay leaf; throw away the onion and bay leaf.
Add the rice to the simmering stock and cook for 15 minutes until tender. Shred the chicken with two forks while it cooks.

Whisk the eggs in a heatproof bowl until frothy, then whisk in the lemon juice. Turn the soup down to the lowest heat. Ladle in about 250ml of the hot stock, a little at a time, whisking constantly, to warm the eggs without scrambling them.

Pour the egg mixture back into the pan, stirring, then return the chicken. Keep the soup over low heat, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until it thickens slightly and is steaming. Don't let it boil, or the eggs will curdle.
Season with salt, pepper and more lemon to taste, and serve scattered with dill.
notes: Reheat leftovers gently over low heat, stirring, and never let it boil.

recipes.title: Briam
recipes.summary: Greek tray-baked summer vegetables in tomato and plenty of olive oil, slow-roasted until sweet and jammy.

items: 1 red onion, cut into thin wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced).
Put all the vegetables and garlic in a large roasting tin. Add the tomatoes, oil, oregano, salt, pepper and water and toss with your hands until everything is coated. Spread out evenly.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes.
Uncover, stir gently and bake for 30 to 35 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the vegetables are soft and caramelised at the edges.
Rest for 10 minutes, scatter with parsley and serve warm, with feta and bread if you like.
notes: It's even better the next day, at room temperature.
The bread and feta are what make it a meal; without them it's vegan and gluten free.

recipes.title: Menemen
recipes.summary: Turkish breakfast eggs softly scrambled into sweet tomatoes and green peppers, with bread for scooping.
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the capsicum and chilli for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the grated tomato and salt and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, until most of the liquid has cooked off and it's thick and saucy.
Crack in the eggs and leave for 30 seconds, then stir gently with a wooden spoon, folding the eggs through the tomato. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until just set and still soft.
Sprinkle with Aleppo pepper and parsley and serve from the pan with bread, ideally Turkish bread.
notes: Whether onion goes in menemen is a running argument in Turkey. Add half a diced onion with the capsicum if you're on that side.
Softly set eggs aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Cook a minute or two longer until firm.

recipes.title: Lahmacun
recipes.summary: Thin, crisp Turkish flatbreads spread with spiced lamb, then rolled up with parsley, onion and lemon.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the water and oil and bring together, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.

For the topping, blitz the onion, capsicum, tomato, garlic and parsley in a food processor until finely chopped but not puréed. Add the lamb, tomato paste, spices and salt and pulse to a smooth paste. Keep it in the fridge until needed.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan-forced) with two oven trays inside. Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each out on a floured bench as thinly as you can, to about 25 x 15cm.
Lay two or three bases on a sheet of baking paper and spread each with a thin, even layer of the lamb, right to the edges.
Slide the paper onto a hot tray and bake for 7 to 9 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the lamb is browned and cooked through. Repeat with the rest.
Toss the red onion with the sumac. Serve the lahmacun hot, scattered with onion and parsley and squeezed with lemon, then rolled up to eat.
notes: The lamb layer must be thin so it cooks through in the short bake. If yours is thicker, give it a couple of minutes more.

image.credit: Photo: Rainer Zenz / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

recipes.title: Imam Bayildi
recipes.summary: Whole eggplants braised in olive oil and stuffed with sweet, slow-cooked onion, garlic and tomato.
steps: Peel the eggplants lengthways in stripes, leaving the stalks on. Make a deep slit down the length of each, without cutting through the ends or the base. Sprinkle with half the salt, inside and out, and leave for 15 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the eggplants for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and starting to soften. Lay them slit-side up in a baking dish.

In the same pan, add 2 tbsp more oil and cook the onions over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until very soft and sweet. Add the garlic for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, then stir in most of the parsley.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced). Open the slits and pack the eggplants with the filling, piling any extra around them. Pour over the water and the remaining oil.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 to 15 minutes more until the eggplants are completely soft.
Cool to warm or room temperature, which is how it's traditionally eaten. Scatter with the remaining parsley and serve with bread.
notes: The name means 'the imam fainted', said to be at how good it was (or at how much olive oil it used).

recipes.title: Spinach and Feta Gözleme
recipes.summary: Thin Turkish griddle breads folded around spinach, feta and onion, cooked crisp in a dry pan with butter.
steps: Mix the flour and salt, add the water and oil and bring together into a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth, then divide into 4 balls, cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, then tip into a sieve and press out the liquid. Cool, then mix with the feta, Aleppo pepper and black pepper.
On a floured bench, roll each ball into a very thin rectangle about 30 x 40cm. Spread a quarter of the filling over one half, fold the other half over and press the edges to seal.
Heat a large dry frying pan or flat griddle over medium heat. Cook one gözleme at a time for 3 minutes a side, brushing the top with melted butter before turning, until crisp and golden in spots.
Cut into pieces and serve hot with lemon wedges.
notes: Swap half the spinach for cooked lamb mince, or add some grated mozzarella for a stretchier filling.

recipes.title: Za'atar Manakish
recipes.summary: Lebanese breakfast flatbreads spread with za'atar and olive oil, baked hot and eaten with tomato, cucumber and mint.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the water and oil and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan-forced) with two oven trays inside. Mix the za'atar and olive oil to a loose paste.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into a 20cm round. Lay them on sheets of baking paper and press dimples all over with your fingertips.
Spread each with the za'atar oil, leaving a thin border. Slide onto the hot trays and bake for 7 to 9 minutes until the edges are golden and the base is crisp.
Serve warm, folded around tomato, cucumber, mint and labneh.
notes: With the labneh left out, they're vegan.

recipes.title: Musakhan
recipes.summary: Palestinian roast chicken on flatbread, under a deep layer of sumac-stained onions and toasted pine nuts.
steps: Rub the chicken with the sumac, allspice, cinnamon, cumin, salt, lemon juice and oil. Leave for 20 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced). Roast the chicken skin-side up on a tray for 50 to 60 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the chicken is cooked through (75°C at the thickest part near the bone).

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat and cook the onions with the salt for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and sweet but only lightly coloured. Stir in the sumac.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, shaking, until golden. Watch them, as they burn quickly.

Lay the breads on two trays and brush with some of the onion oil. Spread with the onions, sit the chicken on top and spoon over any pan juices. Return to the oven for 5 to 8 minutes, until the bread edges are crisp.
Scatter with pine nuts and parsley and serve, tearing the bread to eat with the chicken.
notes: In Palestine it's made with taboon bread. Large Lebanese bread is the closest at the supermarket.

recipes.title: Baked Kibbeh
recipes.summary: A tray of spiced lamb and bulgur, layered around a pine nut and onion filling and baked until crisp-edged.
steps: Rinse the bulgur in a sieve, then soak in cold water for 15 minutes. Drain and squeeze out as much water as you can.

For the filling, heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onions for 8 minutes until soft. Add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the pine nuts, spices and salt and cook for 2 minutes. Cool.

For the shell, blitz the onion in a food processor until fine. Add the bulgur, lamb, spices, salt and pepper and process, adding the iced water a spoonful at a time, until it forms a smooth, sticky paste (do it in two batches if your processor is small).

Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan-forced) and oil a 23 x 33cm baking dish. With wet hands, press half the shell mixture evenly over the base. Spread over the filling, then cover with the rest of the shell, patting it out in pieces and smoothing the joins with wet fingers.
Score the top into diamonds, cutting right through to the base. Drizzle the olive oil over and into the cuts.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep brown at the edges and cooked through (75°C in the centre). Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with the yoghurt mixed with cucumber.
notes: Fine bulgur is essential for the shell. Coarse bulgur won't bind.

recipes.title: Muhammara
recipes.summary: A smoky, sweet-sour Syrian dip of roasted capsicum, walnuts and pomegranate molasses.

items: 4 pita breads, warmed and cut into wedges

steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking, until fragrant. Set a few aside for the top.
Pat the capsicum dry with paper towel. Put it in a food processor with the walnuts, breadcrumbs, garlic, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice, cumin, Aleppo pepper and salt.
Pulse to a thick, slightly coarse paste. With the motor running, drizzle in 3 tbsp of the oil.
Taste and adjust: it should be sweet, sour, smoky and gently hot. Spread on a plate, drizzle with the remaining oil and top with the reserved walnuts, roughly chopped. Serve with warm pita.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days and is good with grilled meat as well as on bread.

recipes.title: Kefta Tagine with Eggs
recipes.summary: Moroccan spiced beef meatballs simmered in a cumin and tomato sauce, finished with eggs baked in the pan.
steps: Mix all the kefta ingredients with your hands until well combined. Roll into small balls, about 2.5cm across (you'll get about 30).
For the sauce, heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan with a lid (or a tagine) over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, water and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Drop the meatballs into the sauce in a single layer. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, turning them once, until cooked through (75°C in the centre).
Make 4 hollows in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are as you like them.
Scatter with coriander and serve from the pan, with bread for scooping.
notes: Runny yolks aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Cook covered until the yolks are firm.
Lamb mince, or half lamb and half beef, works just as well.

image.credit: Photo: Mzximvs VdB / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Koshari
recipes.summary: Egypt's street-food staple: lentils, rice and macaroni under a sharp tomato sauce and a heap of crisp onions.

items: 3 brown onions, halved and thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and crisp. Lift out with a slotted spoon onto paper towel, sprinkle with the salt and keep the oil.
Meanwhile, cover the lentils with plenty of water in a saucepan, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes, until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the onion oil in the same saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the rice and cumin for 1 minute, then add the lentils, salt and 500ml water. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Cook the macaroni in a pot of boiling salted water until tender, adding the chickpeas for the last minute to warm through. Drain.

For the sauce, heat 1 tablespoon of the onion oil in a saucepan over medium heat and fry the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute. Add the passata, vinegar, sugar and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir the garlic vinegar ingredients together.
To serve, fluff the rice and lentils and spoon into bowls. Top with macaroni and chickpeas, plenty of tomato sauce and a pile of crisp onions. Pass the garlic vinegar at the table.
notes: The onions are the point, so take them properly brown. Pull them out a shade before you think they're done; they keep darkening off the heat.
Cooked rice shouldn't sit out at room temperature for long. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

image.credit: Photo: Dina Said / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Moroccan Carrot Salad
recipes.summary: Just-tender carrots dressed while warm with cumin, paprika, garlic and lemon, then heaped with fresh herbs.

items: 600g carrots, peeled and cut into 5mm rounds
Handful of flat-leaf parsley leaves, chopped

steps: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the carrots and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until just tender but still with a little bite. Drain well.
While the carrots cook, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, honey and salt in a large bowl.
Tip the hot carrots into the dressing and toss. Leave for at least 10 minutes so they soak it up as they cool.
Stir through the herbs just before serving, warm or at room temperature.
notes: It keeps for 2 days in the fridge and tastes better on the second. Add the herbs on the day you eat it.
Good alongside grilled lamb, chicken or a pile of flatbreads and hummus.

recipes.title: Harcha
recipes.summary: Moroccan semolina griddle breads, crumbly and buttery, split warm and spread with butter and honey.
steps: Mix the fine semolina, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Pour in the melted butter and rub it through with your fingers until the mixture looks like damp sand.
Add the warm milk and bring it together into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Don't knead it. Cover and rest for 10 minutes so the semolina can soak up the liquid.
Divide into 8 balls. Flatten each between your palms into a round about 1cm thick and press both sides into the coarse semolina.

Heat a heavy frying pan over medium-low heat with no oil. Cook the harcha in batches for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until golden and cooked through. Keep the heat gentle; they burn before the middle cooks if it's too high.
Serve warm, split open and spread with butter and honey.
notes: They're best within a few hours. Leftovers warm up well in a dry pan.
For a savoury version, leave out the sugar and serve with soft cheese.

recipes.title: Chicken Yassa
recipes.summary: Senegalese chicken marinated in lemon and mustard, braised in a pot of sweet, slow-cooked onions.

items: 1 scotch bonnet chilli, pierced with a knife (or 1 long red chilli)

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper in a large bowl. Add the chicken and onions and toss well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade and pat the skin dry. Drain the onions in a sieve over a bowl, keeping the liquid.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 6 to 8 minutes until golden, turn for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onions. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring often, until soft, sweet and lightly golden.

Pour in the saved marinade and the stock, and add the bay leaf and whole chilli. Bring to the boil. Nestle the chicken in skin-side up, cover and simmer gently for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (75°C at the bone). Stir in the olives for the last 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Take out the chilli and bay leaf and serve the chicken and onions over the rice.
notes: The raw-chicken marinade is safe here because it's boiled in the pot before the chicken goes back in.
Scotch bonnets are fierce. Left whole and pierced they give fragrance and moderate heat; chop one in if you like it hot.

recipes.title: Red Red
recipes.summary: Ghanaian black-eyed bean stew in a gingery tomato sauce, served with sweet fried plantain.

items: 1 scotch bonnet chilli, finely chopped (or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes)
800g tinned black-eyed beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the beans and salt and simmer for 10 minutes more, stirring now and then, until thick. Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to help it along.

Meanwhile, peel the plantains and cut them on an angle into 1cm slices. Heat 1cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until deep golden and caramelised. Drain on paper towel and sprinkle with salt.
Spoon the beans into bowls, scatter with spring onion and serve with the plantain.
notes: The name comes from the red palm oil the stew is made with, and the red of the plantain. If you find red palm oil at an African grocer, use it instead of the neutral oil.
Plantains need to be yellow with lots of black spots to fry sweet and soft. Green ones are starchy and suit boiling instead.

recipes.title: Puff-Puff
recipes.summary: Soft, golden West African doughnut balls, lightly sweet with a hint of nutmeg.
steps: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar, nutmeg and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm water and beat with a wooden spoon or your hand for 2 to 3 minutes into a thick, smooth, sticky batter.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1 hour, until doubled and full of bubbles.
Heat 5cm of oil in a heavy saucepan to 170°C. Use a thermometer if you have one; a small blob of batter should sizzle and rise straight away.

Scoop up a walnut-sized piece of batter with a wet tablespoon and push it into the oil with another wet spoon. Fry 6 to 8 at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden all over. Break the first one open to check the middle is cooked.
Drain on paper towel and dust with icing sugar if you like. Best eaten warm.
notes: Never leave hot oil unattended, keep the pan on a back burner, and let the oil cool completely before moving it.
If they brown before the middle cooks, the oil is too hot. Let it drop back to 170°C.

recipes.title: Kelewele
recipes.summary: Ghana's spiced fried plantain: ripe cubes tossed in ginger and chilli, fried until caramelised.

items: 4 ripe plantains, yellow with black spots

steps: Peel the plantains and cut into 2cm cubes.
Mix the ginger, onion, cayenne, nutmeg and salt in a bowl. Add the plantain, toss to coat and leave for 15 minutes.
Heat 3cm of oil in a heavy saucepan to 175°C. Fry the plantain in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and caramelised at the edges.
Lift out onto paper towel. Serve hot with the peanuts on the side.
notes: Riper plantains caramelise more but soak up more oil and stick together. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot.
Never leave hot oil unattended, and let it cool completely before moving the pan.

recipes.title: Sosaties
recipes.summary: Cape Malay lamb skewers with dried apricots, marinated overnight in a sweet-sour curry sauce.

items: 1kg boneless lamb leg, cut into 3cm cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, curry powder and turmeric and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the jam, vinegar, sugar, bay leaves, salt and water and simmer for 5 minutes. Cool completely.
Put the lamb and apricots in a bowl, pour over the cold marinade and mix. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight. If using bamboo skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes.
Thread the lamb, apricots and red onion onto skewers. Tip the leftover marinade into a small saucepan.
Cook the skewers on a barbecue or chargrill pan over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred outside and cooked to your liking.
Meanwhile, bring the leftover marinade to the boil and let it bubble for 3 minutes to make a sauce. Cook the rice. Serve the skewers on the rice with the sauce spooned over.
notes: The marinade has had raw meat in it, so always boil it for a few minutes before using it as a sauce.
Lamb leg cubes are fine served slightly pink in the middle. Cook longer if you prefer them well done.

recipes.title: Tomato Bredie
recipes.summary: A slow South African lamb and tomato stew, warmly spiced with cinnamon and ginger, with potatoes cooked in.

items: 1.2kg bone-in lamb shoulder chops, cut into large pieces

steps: Season the lamb with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb in batches, 5 minutes a batch. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cloves and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and water, scraping up the browned bits. Return the lamb and its juices. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low heat for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then.

Add the potatoes, pushing them under the sauce. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes more, until the lamb is falling off the bone and the potatoes are tender. If the sauce is thin, simmer uncovered for the last 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Take out the cinnamon stick, taste for salt and serve the bredie over the rice.
notes: Like most stews it's better the next day. Cool it quickly, refrigerate within an hour and reheat until bubbling.
Use ripe summer tomatoes if you can. In winter, swap half for a 400g tin of chopped tomatoes.

recipes.title: Chakalaka and Pap
recipes.summary: South Africa's spicy vegetable and bean relish, served on soft, steaming maize porridge.
steps: For the chakalaka, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, chilli and curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Add both capsicums and the carrots and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Stir in the baked beans and salt and simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Taste for salt and heat.

Meanwhile, make the pap. Bring the water and salt to the boil in a heavy saucepan. Whisking all the time, pour in the polenta in a slow, steady stream. Turn the heat to low and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until thick and smooth. Stir in the butter if using. It spits as it cooks, so keep a lid half on.
Spoon the pap into bowls and top with the chakalaka. It's good hot, warm or at room temperature.
notes: Instant polenta cooks in about 5 minutes; follow the packet. White maize meal from an African grocer gives the most authentic pap.
Chakalaka is also the classic side at a braai, next to sausages and chops.

recipes.title: Vetkoek with Curried Mince
recipes.summary: Golden fried bread puffs, split while hot and stuffed with gently curried beef mince.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add the water and knead for 5 to 8 minutes into a smooth, soft dough. Cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1 hour, until doubled.

Meanwhile, make the mince. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute, then the mince. Turn the heat up and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over.

Add the carrot, tomatoes, tomato paste, chutney and water. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes. The mince should be cooked through with no pink left (75°C). Season with the salt and keep warm.
Knock back the dough and divide into 12 balls. Flatten each slightly and rest on a floured tray for 15 minutes.

Heat 4cm of oil in a heavy saucepan to 170°C. Fry 3 or 4 at a time for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until deep golden and they sound hollow when tapped. Break the first one open to check the middle is cooked. Drain on paper towel.
Split each vetkoek while warm and fill with curried mince.
notes: If they brown too fast and stay doughy inside, the oil is too hot. Let it come back down to 170°C.
Never leave hot oil unattended, and let it cool completely before moving the pan.
Vetkoek are also good with butter and golden syrup, or cheese and apricot jam.

recipes.title: Upma
recipes.summary: A South Indian breakfast of toasted semolina cooked soft with mustard seeds, curry leaves, cashews and vegetables.
steps: Toast the semolina in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty but hasn't coloured. Tip onto a plate.
Heat the ghee in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and, once they pop, the cumin seeds, curry leaves and cashews. Stir for 1 minute until the cashews are golden.
Add the onion, chilli and ginger and cook for 4 minutes until soft. Add the carrot and peas and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, add the salt and bring to the boil. Turn the heat to low and pour in the semolina in a slow stream, stirring all the time so it doesn't lump.
Cover and cook for 3 minutes, then stir. It should be soft and fluffy. Stir through the lemon juice and coriander and serve hot.
notes: Use the coarser semolina if your supermarket has a choice; Indian grocers sell it as rava or sooji.
Upma firms up as it cools. Loosen leftovers with a splash of hot water when reheating.

recipes.title: Pork Vindaloo
recipes.summary: Goan pork shoulder marinated in a chilli, garlic and vinegar paste, then braised until tender and tangy.

items: 8 dried Kashmiri chillies, stemmed and seeded

steps: Soak the chillies in just-boiled water for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, toast the cumin seeds, peppercorns and cinnamon stick in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Drain the chillies and blend them with the toasted spices (break up the cinnamon), the cloves, turmeric, garlic, ginger, vinegar, sugar and salt to a smooth paste.
Rub the paste all over the pork in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onions for 12 minutes, until golden. Add the pork and all its paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the tomatoes and water and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then, until the pork is very tender. Uncover and simmer for 15 minutes more to thicken.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Taste the curry for salt and serve.
notes: Kashmiri chillies give colour more than fire, so this is warm rather than blistering. Add 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper to the paste for a hotter vindaloo.
It improves overnight. Cool quickly, refrigerate within an hour and reheat until bubbling.

recipes.title: Rajma
recipes.summary: Punjabi red kidney beans simmered in a thick, gently spiced onion and tomato gravy, made for rice.

items: 800g tinned red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the ghee in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and bay leaf and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onions and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden. Add the ginger garlic paste and green chilli and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the ground coriander, chilli powder and turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes, until thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add the beans, water and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Crush the fenugreek leaves between your palms into the rajma, add the garam masala and simmer for 2 minutes. Scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.
notes: To cook from dried beans, soak 250g overnight, then boil hard for 10 minutes and simmer until soft (about 1 hour). Raw or undercooked kidney beans are toxic, so never slow-cook them from raw.
Rajma chawal (with rice) is the classic, but it's also good with roti.

recipes.title: Onion Bhaji
recipes.summary: Crisp, lacy tangles of spiced onion in chickpea batter, fried golden and served with mint chutney.

items: 3 brown onions, halved and thinly sliced

steps: Toss the onions with the salt in a large bowl and leave for 10 minutes, until they soften and release some liquid.

Add the chickpea flour, rice flour, cumin seeds, turmeric, chilli powder, green chilli, ginger and coriander. Mix with your hands, then add the water a little at a time until the onions are coated in a thick, sticky batter. You may not need it all.
Heat 4cm of oil in a heavy saucepan to 170°C. Drop in loose spoonfuls of the mixture, 4 or 5 at a time, and fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot with mint chutney.
notes: Keep them loose and craggy rather than pressing them into balls; the straggly edges are the crispest part.
Never leave hot oil unattended, and let it cool completely before moving the pan.

recipes.title: Panang Beef Curry
recipes.summary: A thick, rich Thai curry of tender beef in coconut cream, sweet with peanut and fragrant with lime leaves.

items: 600g beef rump steak, thinly sliced across the grain
4 makrut lime leaves, very finely shredded

steps: Start the rice cooking.
Put half the coconut cream in a wok or wide pan over medium heat and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and the oil starts to separate.
Add the curry paste and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in the peanut butter, palm sugar and fish sauce.

Add the beef, the rest of the coconut cream and most of the lime leaves. Simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes, until the beef is just cooked and the sauce is thick enough to coat it. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Taste and balance with more fish sauce or sugar. Scatter with the chilli, Thai basil and remaining lime leaves and serve with the rice.
notes: If you find panang curry paste, use it instead of the red curry paste and halve the peanut butter. Red curry paste with peanut is a common stand-in.
Slice the beef more easily by putting it in the freezer for 20 minutes first.

image.credit: Photo: Vee Satayamas / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

recipes.title: Gai Yang
recipes.summary: Isaan-style grilled chicken marinated in garlic, coriander root and lemongrass, with a smoky chilli dipping sauce.

items: 2 lemongrass stalks, white part finely chopped

steps: Pound the coriander roots, garlic and peppercorns to a rough paste with a mortar and pestle (or blitz in a small food processor). Add the lemongrass and pound briefly, then stir in the fish sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar and oil.
Slash the chicken a couple of times through the thickest part, rub the marinade all over and into the cuts, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Heat a barbecue to medium, or the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced). Grill the chicken for 30 to 40 minutes, turning often and moving it to a cooler spot if it chars too fast, or roast on a rack over a tray for 35 to 40 minutes. It's done when cooked through (75°C at the bone).
Meanwhile, cook the rice and stir the dipping sauce ingredients together.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then serve with the rice and the dipping sauce.
notes: Coriander roots carry most of the flavour. Buy coriander with roots on; if yours has none, use 2 tbsp chopped stems.
Toasted rice powder (khao khua) is sold at Asian grocers. To make it, toast raw sticky or jasmine rice in a dry pan until deep golden, then grind.

recipes.title: Yum Woon Sen
recipes.summary: A Thai glass noodle salad with pork and prawns, tossed in a hot, sour and salty lime dressing.

items: 2 celery stalks, thinly sliced on an angle

steps: Soak the noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable. Drop into a pot of boiling water for 1 minute, drain, rinse under cold water and snip into shorter lengths with scissors.
Put the pork mince and water in a small frying pan over medium heat. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it's cooked through.
Add the prawns to the pan and cook for 2 minutes, until pink and opaque.
Stir the dressing ingredients together in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves. Add the noodles, warm pork and prawns, shallots, celery and tomatoes and toss well.
Toss through the spring onions and coriander, scatter with peanuts and serve on lettuce leaves.
notes: The warm pork and prawns help the noodles soak up the dressing. Taste and adjust: it should be sour first, then salty, hot and only a little sweet.
Chinese celery, from Asian grocers, is more authentic; use the leaves too.

recipes.title: Khai Jiao
recipes.summary: The Thai omelette: eggs whisked frothy and fried in hot oil until puffed and crisp, served on rice with sriracha.
steps: Whisk the eggs, fish sauce, lime juice and rice flour hard for 1 minute, until very frothy. Stir in the spring onion.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering (about 180°C). A drop of egg should puff up immediately.
Pour in half the egg from a little height, away from you. It will puff and bubble at once. Cook for about 1 minute, until crisp and golden underneath, then flip carefully and cook for 1 minute more.
Lift out onto paper towel and repeat with the rest of the egg.
Serve each omelette on a mound of hot rice with sriracha and coriander.
notes: Hot oil spits when the egg goes in. Keep your face and hands back, and let the oil cool completely before moving the wok.
The omelette is cooked through, so it's fine for everyone.

image.credit: Photo: Sakurai Midori / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.5)

recipes.title: Bun Cha
recipes.summary: Hanoi's chargrilled pork patties and pork belly in a warm, sweet-sour dipping broth, with noodles and herbs.

items: 400g pork belly, rind removed, thinly sliced

steps: Mix the shallots, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, pepper and oil. Put half in a bowl with the pork mince and half with the pork belly. Mix each well, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Stir the dipping broth ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Cook the noodles according to the packet, then rinse under cold water and drain well.

Shape the mince into 16 small, flat patties. Heat a barbecue, chargrill pan or overhead grill to high. Cook the patties for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until charred and cooked through (75°C in the centre). Cook the belly slices for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until caramelised and cooked through.
Divide the warm broth between four bowls and drop in the hot pork. Serve with the noodles, lettuce, herbs and bean sprouts, so everyone can dip noodles and greens into their broth.
notes: Grilling over charcoal gives the real Hanoi smokiness, but a very hot chargrill pan does a good job.
Ask the butcher to slice the belly thinly, or freeze it for 30 minutes and slice it yourself.

image.credit: Photo: Phương Huy / Wikimedia Commons (public domain)

recipes.title: Banh Xeo
recipes.summary: Crisp Vietnamese turmeric and coconut pancakes filled with pork, prawns and bean sprouts, wrapped in lettuce and herbs.

items: 300g pork belly, rind removed, thinly sliced

steps: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric, salt, coconut milk and soda water to a thin batter, like pouring cream. Stir in the spring onions and rest for 30 minutes.
Stir the dipping sauce ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over high heat. Add an eighth of the pork and a few onion slices and fry for 2 minutes, until the pork is cooked through. Add an eighth of the prawns.

Stir the batter, then pour in about 80ml and swirl the pan so it coats the base thinly. Cover and cook for 2 minutes. Scatter a handful of bean sprouts over one half, uncover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the edges are lacy and the base is golden and crisp. The prawns should be pink and opaque.
Fold in half and slide onto a plate. Repeat with the rest, stirring the batter each time and keeping cooked ones warm in a low oven.
To eat, break off pieces of pancake, wrap in lettuce with herbs and dip in the sauce.
notes: A hot pan and a thin layer of batter are what make it crisp. The first one is often a tester.
Use any combination of pork, prawns or mushrooms for the filling.

recipes.title: Caramelised Ginger Chicken
recipes.summary: Vietnamese ga kho gung: chicken thigh cooked down in a dark caramel with plenty of ginger and fish sauce.

items: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 4cm pieces
50g ginger, peeled and cut into fine matchsticks

steps: Mix the chicken with the fish sauce, pepper and half the garlic and leave for 15 minutes. Start the rice.
Put the sugar in a large frying pan or wide saucepan over medium heat. Leave it to melt without stirring, swirling the pan now and then, for 4 to 5 minutes until it's a deep amber caramel.
Carefully add the oil, ginger, shallots and remaining garlic (the caramel will spit) and stir for 1 minute.

Add the chicken and its marinade and toss for 3 minutes to coat. Pour in the water and simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is sticky and dark and the chicken is cooked through (75°C).
Scatter with spring onion and chilli and serve with the rice.
notes: Hot caramel burns badly. Keep children away from the stove and add the oil and aromatics at arm's length.
Take the caramel as dark as you dare without it smelling burnt; that bitterness is what balances the sweetness.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Chicken Salad
recipes.summary: Poached chicken, crunchy cabbage and lots of herbs in a sharp lime dressing, with peanuts and fried shallots.
steps: Put the chicken in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add the salt. Bring to a bare simmer, cook for 10 minutes, then turn off the heat, cover and leave for 15 minutes, until cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Lift out and cool, then shred.
Meanwhile, toss the red onion with the vinegar and leave for 10 minutes to soften its bite. Drain.
Stir the dressing ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the chicken, onion, wombok, carrot and herbs with the dressing.
Pile onto a platter and scatter with the peanuts and fried shallots.
notes: Dress it just before serving so the cabbage stays crunchy.
A shredded barbecue chicken makes this a 15-minute lunch.

recipes.title: Dan Dan Noodles
recipes.summary: Sichuan noodles in a numbing, nutty chilli and sesame sauce, topped with crisp seasoned pork.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok or frying pan over high heat. Add the pork and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned, crisp in places and cooked through. Add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces and the mustard greens and stir-fry for 2 minutes more.
Divide the sauce ingredients between four bowls and stir each into a smooth sauce.
Cook the noodles in a large pot of boiling water according to the packet, adding the bok choy for the last minute. Drain.
Divide the noodles and bok choy between the bowls and top with the pork, spring onions and peanuts. Toss everything together at the table.
notes: Chinese sesame paste is made from toasted sesame and is more traditional; tahini works well. Stir the jar well first.
Pickled mustard greens (ya cai or suan cai) are sold in packets at Asian grocers. Leave them out if you can't find them.

recipes.title: Hot and Sour Soup
recipes.summary: A silky Chinese soup with pork, shiitake, tofu and egg ribbons, sharp with black vinegar and hot with white pepper.

items: 150g pork fillet, cut into thin matchsticks
150g firm tofu, cut into thin strips

steps: Soak the shiitake in the boiling water for 20 minutes. Squeeze them out, keeping the liquid, cut off the stems and slice the caps thinly. Meanwhile, mix the pork with the soy sauce and cornflour.
Bring the stock, mushroom liquid (leave any grit behind) and sliced shiitake to the boil in a large saucepan. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the pork, stirring to separate the pieces, and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through. Add the tofu, soy sauce, sugar and salt.
Mix the cornflour with the cold water, stir it into the soup and simmer for 1 minute until glossy and slightly thickened.
Turn the heat to low. Pour in the eggs in a thin stream while stirring the soup slowly in one direction, so they set in ribbons. Take off the heat.
Stir in both vinegars, the white pepper, sesame oil and chilli oil. Taste: it should be sour and peppery. Serve topped with spring onion.
notes: Add the vinegar and pepper off the heat; boiling dulls them.
Sliced bamboo shoots and wood ear mushrooms from an Asian grocer are traditional additions. Add them with the tofu.

recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli
recipes.summary: Tender, velveted beef and crisp broccoli in a glossy oyster and garlic sauce, faster than takeaway.

items: 500g beef rump, trimmed and thinly sliced across the grain
1 large head broccoli, cut into small florets

steps: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornflour and 1 tbsp oil. Leave for 15 minutes while you prepare everything else.
Whisk the sauce ingredients together until the cornflour dissolves.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Add the broccoli and 3 tbsp water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Tip onto a plate.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the hot wok and spread half the beef out in one layer. Sear for 1 minute without moving, then toss for 30 seconds more and lift out. Repeat with the rest of the oil and beef.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic, ginger and spring onion and stir for 30 seconds. Whisk the sauce again, pour it in and bubble for 1 minute until thick and glossy.
Return the beef and broccoli and toss for 1 minute to coat and heat through. Serve straight away with rice.
notes: Slicing across the grain and cooking in two batches is what keeps the beef tender. A crowded wok stews the meat.
Put the beef in the freezer for 20 minutes first and it slices thinly far more easily.

recipes.title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
recipes.summary: Cold, crunchy smashed cucumbers in a garlicky black vinegar and chilli oil dressing.
steps: Lay a cucumber on a board and whack it along its length with the flat of a large knife or a rolling pin until it cracks open. Cut it into 3cm chunks on an angle. Repeat with the rest.
Toss the cucumber with the salt and sugar in a colander and leave over a bowl for 15 minutes to draw out the water. Shake off the liquid and tip into a serving bowl.
Mix the garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, chilli oil and sesame oil.
Pour the dressing over the cucumber and toss. Scatter with sesame seeds and coriander and serve cold, within an hour.
notes: Smashing rather than slicing gives rough edges that hold far more dressing.
Black vinegar and soy sauce both contain wheat, so this isn't gluten-free. Use tamari and rice vinegar if you need it to be.

image.credit: Photo: Daniela Eftimova / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Onigiri
recipes.summary: Japanese rice balls with a tuna-mayo centre, wrapped in crisp nori. Lunchbox gold.

items: 185g tin tuna in olive oil, well drained

steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water, rubbing it with your hand, until the water runs almost clear. Put it in a saucepan with the water and soak for 10 minutes.

Bring to the boil, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Spread onto a tray to cool until warm enough to handle, about 10 minutes.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, soy sauce and spring onion.

Wet your hands and rub them with a little of the salt. Take about 100g of rice, flatten it in your palm and put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle. Close the rice over the filling and press firmly into a triangle, turning it in your cupped hands. Make 8.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and wrap a half sheet of nori around the base of each just before eating, so it stays crisp.
notes: Shape the rice while it's still warm, or it won't stick together. Once made, eat within a few hours or refrigerate and eat the same day. Cooked rice shouldn't sit at room temperature for long.
Packed for lunch, keep the onigiri in an insulated bag with an ice brick, and the nori separate so it doesn't go soggy.

recipes.title: Tamagoyaki
recipes.summary: A sweet-savoury rolled Japanese omelette, cooked in thin layers for soft, neat slices.
steps: Beat the eggs gently with chopsticks, cutting through the whites rather than whipping in air. Stir in the dashi, sugar, mirin, soy sauce and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Heat a small frying pan (a square tamagoyaki pan if you have one) over medium-low heat. Wipe it with oil using folded paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer of egg, tilting to cover the base. When it's just set on the bottom but still a little wet on top, roll it from the far side towards you with chopsticks or a spatula.

Push the roll to the far side, wipe the empty pan with oil and pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg runs underneath. When nearly set, roll it back towards you around the first roll. Repeat until the egg is used up.
Tip the omelette onto a bamboo mat or a clean tea towel, wrap and press gently into a neat block. Rest for 2 minutes, then slice and serve warm or at room temperature with rice and pickled ginger.
notes: Keep the heat low. Browning makes it tough and the sugar catches quickly.
It keeps in the fridge for a day and is a lunchbox favourite in Japan.

image.credit: Photo: 極地狐 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

recipes.title: Nikujaga
recipes.summary: Japanese home-style beef and potato stew, simmered in a sweet soy and dashi broth.

items: 300g beef scotch fillet, very thinly sliced
1 brown onion, cut into thin wedges
700g potatoes, peeled and cut into large chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a wide saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until it just changes colour. Add the onion and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and carrot and stir to coat. Pour in the dashi and bring to the boil, skimming off any foam.
Add the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar. Lay a piece of baking paper or a small lid directly on the surface and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender but holding their shape.
Remove the paper, add the snow peas and simmer for 2 minutes more. Turn off the heat and leave for 5 minutes so the potatoes soak up the broth. Serve in bowls with some of the broth, with rice.
notes: Asian grocers and many supermarkets sell shabu-shabu or sukiyaki beef already sliced paper-thin, which saves time.
It's even better the next day, once the potatoes have soaked up more flavour. Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

image.credit: Photo: ノボホショコロトソ / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

recipes.title: Chicken Karaage
recipes.summary: Ginger and soy marinated chicken thigh, double-fried in a potato starch coat until shatteringly crisp.

items: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 4cm pieces

steps: Mix the chicken with the soy sauce, sake, ginger, garlic and sugar. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
Pour the oil into a large, heavy saucepan no more than one-third full and heat to 170°C on a cooking thermometer. Keep a lid nearby and never leave the pan.
Drain the chicken and toss a few pieces at a time in the potato starch, shaking off the excess.
Fry in batches of 6 to 8 pieces for 3 minutes, until pale golden. Lift onto a wire rack. Let the oil come back to 170°C between batches.

When it's all fried once, heat the oil to 190°C and fry the pieces again in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until deep golden and very crisp, and cooked through (75°C in the centre of the largest piece). Drain on the rack.
Serve hot with lettuce, Kewpie mayonnaise and lemon wedges.
notes: The rest between the two fries lets heat reach the centre, and the second hot fry dries the crust so it stays crisp.
Let the oil cool completely in the pan before straining it for reuse or disposing of it.

recipes.title: Japchae
recipes.summary: Chewy sweet potato noodles tossed with beef, vegetables and sesame in a sweet soy dressing.

items: 250g beef rump, cut into thin strips

steps: Mix the sauce ingredients. Toss the beef with 1 tbsp of the sauce.

Cook the noodles in a large saucepan of boiling water for 6 minutes, until soft and chewy. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well. Snip into shorter lengths with kitchen scissors and toss with 2 tbsp of the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the onion and carrot for 2 minutes, then the capsicum for 1 minute. Tip into a large bowl.
Stir-fry the mushrooms for 2 minutes and add to the bowl. Wilt the spinach for 30 seconds and add to the bowl.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the beef for 2 minutes until browned and cooked. Add to the bowl.

Put the noodles and spring onion in the wok with the rest of the sauce and toss over medium heat for 2 minutes until hot. Tip into the bowl and toss everything together with your hands or tongs. Scatter with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Cooking each vegetable separately keeps the colours bright and nothing goes soggy.
For a vegetarian version, leave out the beef and add 200g sliced firm tofu, pan-fried until golden.

image.credit: Photo: Alan Chan / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Pajeon
recipes.summary: A crisp Korean spring onion pancake, served in wedges with a tangy soy dipping sauce.

items: 2 bunches spring onions, cut into 10cm lengths

steps: Mix the dipping sauce ingredients and set aside.
Whisk the flour, potato starch, salt, egg and cold water to a smooth, thin batter.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Lay half the spring onions in the pan in a single layer, all facing the same way. Pour over half the batter to just coat them, and scatter with half the chilli.
Cook for 4 minutes, pressing down with a spatula, until golden and crisp underneath. Flip and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, adding a little more oil around the edge, until crisp.
Slide onto a board and repeat with the rest. Cut into wedges and serve hot with the dipping sauce.
notes: Cold water and a hot, well-oiled pan are what make it crisp rather than doughy.
For haemul pajeon, scatter 150g chopped raw prawns or squid over the spring onions before adding the batter, and cook until the seafood is opaque.

recipes.title: Gimbap
recipes.summary: Korean seaweed rice rolls with egg, ham, spinach, carrot and pickled radish, sliced into rounds.

items: 3 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
1 Lebanese cucumber, cut into long batons

steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then put it in a saucepan with the water and soak for 10 minutes. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest covered for 10 minutes. Gently mix in the sesame oil, salt and sesame seeds and spread on a tray to cool until just warm.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat and cook the eggs as a thin omelette until set. Roll up and cut into long strips.

Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, rinse under cold water and squeeze dry. Toss with the sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Stir-fry the carrot in a little oil for 2 minutes with a pinch of salt. Lightly fry the ham strips for 1 minute.
Lay a nori sheet shiny side down on a bamboo mat. Spread a quarter of the rice thinly over it, leaving a 3cm strip bare at the far edge.

Lay a quarter of each filling in neat lines across the middle of the rice. Using the mat, roll up firmly from the near side, pressing as you go, and seal the bare edge with a few grains of rice. Repeat with the rest.
Brush the rolls with sesame oil. Slice into 1.5cm rounds with a sharp, wet knife.
notes: Roll while the rice is still slightly warm, then eat within a few hours or refrigerate and eat the same day. For lunchboxes, keep cold with an ice brick.
Yellow pickled radish (danmuji) is sold in long strips at Asian grocers, sometimes in a gimbap pack with burdock.

recipes.title: Dakgalbi
recipes.summary: Spicy gochujang chicken stir-fried with cabbage, sweet potato and chewy rice cakes.

items: 700g chicken thigh fillets, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 sweet potato, peeled, halved and cut into 5mm slices

steps: Mix the marinade, add the chicken and toss. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to a day.
If the rice cakes are hard from the fridge, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the cabbage, sweet potato and onion and stir-fry for 3 minutes.

Add the chicken with all its marinade, the rice cakes and 60ml water. Stir-fry for 10 to 12 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender, the rice cakes are soft and the chicken is cooked through (75°C in the thickest piece). Add a splash more water if it sticks.
Toss through the spring onions for 1 minute, scatter with sesame seeds and serve with rice.
notes: At home in Korea the leftovers are finished by frying rice in the pan with a little kimchi and sesame oil.
Gochujang and soy sauce contain wheat, so this isn't gluten-free.

recipes.title: Nasi Lemak
recipes.summary: Coconut rice with sweet-hot onion sambal, egg, peanuts and cucumber: Malaysia's breakfast.
steps: Soak the dried chillies in just-boiled water for 20 minutes, then drain.

Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear. Put it in a saucepan with the coconut milk, water, ginger and salt, stir and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and remove the ginger.
Meanwhile, blend the soaked chillies, shallots, garlic and shrimp paste with 2 tbsp water to a smooth paste.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat and fry the paste for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens and the oil separates. Add the onion rings and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the tamarind, palm sugar, salt and 60ml water. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick and glossy.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel. Halve them.
Serve the warm rice with a spoonful of sambal, the eggs, peanuts and cucumber.
notes: Traditionally it also comes with crisp-fried ikan bilis (dried anchovies) from Asian grocers. Fry 50g in a little oil until crisp and scatter over.
Serve the rice straight after cooking. If you make it ahead, cool it quickly, refrigerate within an hour and reheat until steaming.
The sambal keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for a week.

recipes.title: Char Kway Teow
recipes.summary: Smoky stir-fried flat rice noodles with prawns, egg, bean sprouts and garlic chives.

items: 1 bunch garlic chives, cut into 4cm lengths

steps: Mix the sauce ingredients. If the noodles are stiff from the fridge, pour hot water over them in a colander and gently separate them with your fingers. Drain well.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking. Add 2 tbsp oil and the garlic and stir for 10 seconds, then add the prawns and fish cake and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the prawns are opaque.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss for 2 minutes, letting the noodles sit for a few seconds at a time so they char at the edges.
Push the noodles to one side, add the rest of the oil and crack in the eggs. Scramble for 30 seconds, then toss everything together.
Add the bean sprouts and chives and toss for 1 minute, until just wilted. Serve straight away.
notes: Cook no more than two serves at a time. A crowded wok can't get hot enough for the smoky 'wok hei' flavour.
Hawkers add sliced Chinese sausage (lap cheong) and cockles. Add 1 sliced lap cheong with the prawns if you find it at an Asian grocer.

recipes.title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.summary: Silky poached chicken with rice cooked in its broth, and chilli and ginger sauces.

items: 1.6kg whole chicken, at room temperature for 30 minutes
600ml chicken stock, from poaching the chicken

steps: Rub the chicken all over with the salt. Put it breast side down in a large pot with the ginger slices and spring onions and cover with cold water by 2cm. Bring to the boil over high heat, skim, then turn to the lowest heat, cover and poach at a bare simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 75°C.
Lift the chicken into a large bowl of iced water for 10 minutes to firm the skin. Drain, rub with sesame oil and rest. Keep the poaching stock hot.

For the rice, heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and fry the garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes. Add 600ml of the hot poaching stock and the salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Blend the chilli sauce ingredients with 2 tbsp poaching stock until fairly smooth.
For the ginger sauce, put the ginger, spring onion and salt in a heatproof bowl. Heat the oil in a small pan until shimmering and pour it over; it will sizzle.
Carve the chicken into pieces. Serve with the rice, cucumber, coriander, a drizzle of dark soy, both sauces, and a small bowl of the hot stock seasoned with salt.
notes: Poaching gently, never boiling hard, is what keeps the meat silky.
Cool any leftover stock quickly, refrigerate and use within 3 days, or freeze.

recipes.title: Sambal Udang
recipes.summary: Prawns cooked in a deep red, sweet, sour and fiery Malaysian chilli sambal.

items: 800g raw prawns, peeled and deveined, tails on

steps: Soak the dried chillies in just-boiled water for 20 minutes and drain. Blend with the fresh chillies, shallots, garlic, shrimp paste and 3 tbsp water to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-low heat. Fry the paste for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until it turns deep red, smells sweet rather than raw and the oil splits away.
Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the tamarind, palm sugar, salt and 80ml water and simmer for 2 minutes. Taste: it should be hot, sweet and sour in balance.
Add the prawns and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until they are pink and opaque all the way through. Serve with rice and cucumber.
notes: Frying the paste slowly until the oil separates is the step that matters. Rushed sambal tastes raw and harsh.
Open a window when frying the paste; the chilli fumes are strong.

recipes.title: Soto Ayam
recipes.summary: Indonesian turmeric chicken soup with glass noodles, egg, bean sprouts and crisp shallots.

items: 2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and tied in a knot

steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, macadamias, turmeric and coriander with 2 tbsp water to a paste. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.

Add the chicken, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal and salt. Bring to the boil, skim, then simmer gently, partly covered, for 35 minutes, until the chicken is very tender and cooked through (75°C at the bone).
Meanwhile, soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes and drain. Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard the bones. Remove the lemongrass, lime leaves and galangal. Return the chicken to the pot and season to taste.
Divide the noodles, bean sprouts and wombok between deep bowls. Ladle over the hot soup and chicken. Top with egg and fried shallots, and serve with lime wedges and sambal.
notes: Macadamias stand in for candlenuts (kemiri), which thicken the broth. Use 4 candlenuts if you find them at an Asian grocer.
Fried shallots are made in shared fryers, so check the packet if you need the dish gluten-free.

recipes.title: Ayam Bakar
recipes.summary: Javanese grilled chicken, simmered first in spiced coconut, then charred with kecap manis.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, chillies, turmeric and coriander to a paste with 2 tbsp water. Heat the oil in a wide, deep frying pan over medium heat and fry the paste for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Cut each maryland in two at the joint. Add the chicken, lemongrass, coconut milk, 2 tbsp of the kecap manis, the salt and 200ml water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 25 minutes, turning once.
Uncover and simmer for 10 minutes more, until the sauce has reduced to a thick coating. Stir in the lime juice and remaining kecap manis.

Heat a barbecue or chargrill pan to medium-high (or the oven grill to high). Grill the chicken for 8 to 10 minutes, turning and basting with the sauce, until sticky and charred in spots and 75°C at the bone.
Serve with rice, cucumber, tomato and sambal, with any extra sauce spooned over.
notes: Simmering first means the chicken is cooked through before it hits the grill, so the sugary glaze can char without burning while you wait.
Kecap manis contains wheat, so this isn't gluten-free.

image.credit: Photo: Nisa usrifatul / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Perkedel
recipes.summary: Indonesian potato fritters, fragrant with fried shallots and nutmeg, dipped in egg and fried golden.

items: 800g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender. Drain well and leave in the hot pan for 2 minutes to steam dry.
Mash until smooth, then mix in the fried shallots, spring onion, celery leaves, nutmeg, white pepper, salt and 1 of the eggs, lightly beaten. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.
With wet hands, shape into 12 patties about 1.5cm thick.
