Beat the other egg in a shallow bowl. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Dip each patty in the egg and fry in batches for 3 minutes each side, until golden. Drain on paper towel.
Serve warm with sweet chilli sauce, or alongside soto ayam or rice.
notes: Floury potatoes such as Sebago or Coliban make the lightest fritters. Waxy ones go gluey.
For the meaty version, fry 150g beef mince until cooked through and mix it into the potato.

recipes.title: Sayur Lodeh
recipes.summary: A gentle Indonesian vegetable curry in turmeric coconut broth, with tofu puffs.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, chilli, macadamias, galangal, turmeric and coriander with 2 tbsp water to a paste.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and fry the paste with the lemongrass and bay leaves for 5 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the carrot and eggplant and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the beans, wombok and tofu puffs, palm sugar and salt and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes more, until all the vegetables are tender. Don't let it boil hard or the coconut milk can split.
Remove the lemongrass and bay leaves, taste for salt and serve in bowls with rice, scattered with fried shallots.
notes: In Java it's usually seasoned with shrimp paste. Add 1/2 tsp with the spice paste if you're not keeping it vegetarian.
Indonesian salam leaves are traditional; bay leaves are the closest supermarket swap.

recipes.title: Tapsilog
recipes.summary: Filipino breakfast of garlicky cured beef, garlic fried rice and a fried egg.

items: 600g cooked white rice, cold from the fridge

steps: Mix the beef with the soy sauce, lime juice, garlic, sugar and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.

For the garlic rice, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat and fry the garlic for 2 to 3 minutes until pale golden. Lift out half for garnish. Add the rice and salt, raise the heat to medium-high and toss for 5 minutes until piping hot. Keep warm.

Heat the oil for the beef in a frying pan over high heat. Lift the beef from the marinade and fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned and caramelised at the edges. Add a splash of the marinade at the end and let it bubble to a glaze.
Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Mix the vinegar and chilli for dipping. Serve the beef with the garlic rice topped with the reserved garlic, a fried egg and sliced tomato.
notes: Calamansi juice is traditional if you find the fruit; lime is the closest swap.
Use rice cooked the day before and cooled in the fridge. Cooked rice shouldn't sit out at room temperature.
Runny yolks aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Fry the eggs until the yolks are firm.

recipes.title: Pork Sinigang
recipes.summary: A sour Filipino tamarind soup of tender pork ribs, radish, beans and greens.

items: 1kg pork spare ribs, cut into single ribs
300g daikon, peeled, halved and sliced 1cm thick

steps: Put the pork in a large pot, cover with the water and bring to the boil. Skim off the foam for the first 5 minutes.
Add the onion, tomatoes and 2 tbsp of the fish sauce. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is tender and pulling from the bone.
Stir in the tamarind, then add the daikon and whole chillies and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the eggplant and beans and simmer for 5 minutes more, until tender.
Taste and add more fish sauce for salt or more tamarind for sourness. It should be clearly sour. Stir in the spinach until just wilted and serve in bowls with rice.
notes: Kangkong (water spinach) is the traditional green; use it if you find it at an Asian grocer.
Packet sinigang mix from Asian grocers can replace the tamarind paste. Most contain flavour enhancers and some contain wheat, so check the label.

recipes.title: Bistek Tagalog
recipes.summary: Filipino beef steak braised briefly in soy and lime, under a tangle of soft onion rings.

items: 2 brown onions, sliced into thick rings

steps: Mix the beef with the soy sauce, lime juice, garlic and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the onion rings for 3 minutes, until just soft but holding their shape. Lift out.
Lift the beef from the marinade, keeping the marinade. Add the rest of the oil to the pan and sear the beef in batches for 1 minute each side until browned. Lift out.
Pour the marinade, sugar and water into the pan and bring to the boil, scraping up the browned bits. Return the beef, lower the heat, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Uncover, return the onions and simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce is slightly reduced. Serve over rice with the sauce.
notes: Calamansi is the classic citrus; lime or lemon is the supermarket swap.
Soy sauce contains wheat; use tamari to make it gluten-free.

image.credit: Photo: Joy D. Ganaden / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Lumpia Shanghai
recipes.summary: Thin, crisp Filipino pork spring rolls, the party favourite, served with sweet chilli sauce.

items: 1 small brown onion, very finely chopped

steps: Mix the filling ingredients well with your hands.

Keep the wrappers under a damp tea towel. Lay one with a corner pointing towards you and spread a heaped tablespoon of filling in a thin log, about 1cm thick, across the near corner. Fold the corner over, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Seal the far corner with a dab of water. Repeat with the rest.
Pour the oil into a large, heavy saucepan no more than one-third full and heat to 170°C. Keep a lid nearby and never leave the pan.
Fry the rolls in batches of 6 for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the filling is cooked through (75°C in the centre). Drain on a wire rack.
Cut in half on an angle if you like and serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.
notes: Keep the filling thin, about the width of a finger, so it cooks through by the time the wrapper is crisp.
Rolled, uncooked lumpia freeze well in a single layer. Fry from frozen at 160°C for 8 to 9 minutes, checking the centre reaches 75°C.

image.credit: Photo: Ralff Nestor Nacor / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Elote
recipes.summary: Mexican street corn: chargrilled cobs slathered in lime mayo, rolled in salty cheese and chilli.

items: 1 lime, zested, then cut into wedges
60g feta, very finely crumbled (or queso fresco)
Small handful of coriander leaves, chopped

steps: Heat a barbecue or chargrill pan over high heat. Brush the corn with oil and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in patches.
Mix the mayonnaise with the lime zest and a squeeze of lime juice.
While the corn is hot, brush it all over with the lime mayo. Roll or sprinkle with the feta, then dust with chilli powder and scatter with coriander and a little salt.
Serve straight away with lime wedges.
notes: Cotija is the cheese used in Mexico. Dry, salty feta crumbled very finely is the closest supermarket match.
For esquites, cut the charred kernels off the cobs and toss everything together in cups.

recipes.title: Molletes
recipes.summary: Open rolls toasted with refried beans and melted cheese, topped with fresh pico de gallo.

items: 2 x 400g tins pinto beans, drained, 60ml liquid kept
4 bread rolls (bolillo or crusty white), split in half

steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then the beans, kept liquid and salt. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing with a potato masher, until thick and mostly smooth.
Mix the pico de gallo ingredients and set aside.
Heat the oven grill to high. Pull out a little of the soft crumb from each roll half, spread the cut sides thinly with butter and toast under the grill for 2 minutes until golden at the edges.
Spread each half thickly with beans and top with cheese. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Spoon pico de gallo over the top and serve straight away.
notes: Bolillo rolls are traditional; any crusty white roll works.
Good with a fried egg on top, or a spoonful of salsa verde.

recipes.title: Sopa de Fideo
recipes.summary: Toasted thin noodles simmered in a tomato and chicken broth, finished with avocado and lime.
steps: Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic with 250ml of the stock until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the broken pasta and fry, stirring constantly, for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden brown. Watch it closely; it turns quickly.
Pour in the tomato mixture carefully, as it will spit, and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it darkens slightly.
Add the rest of the stock, the oregano and salt. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the pasta is soft. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with avocado, coriander, jalapeño if using and a squeeze of lime.
notes: Mexican fideo noodles are sold in some supermarkets' international aisles; broken spaghettini is the same idea.
Use vegetable stock to make it vegetarian.

recipes.title: Birria Tacos
recipes.summary: Chilli-braised beef in crisp, cheesy tortillas fried in the stew's red fat, with the broth for dipping.

items: 4 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed
3 dried ancho chillies, stems and seeds removed
1.5kg beef chuck, cut into 4 large pieces

steps: Toast the dried chillies in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 30 seconds a side, until they smell fragrant but haven't blackened. Put them in a bowl, cover with boiling water and soak for 20 minutes.
Season the beef with the salt. Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole over medium-high heat and brown the beef well on all sides, in batches, about 8 minutes. Set aside.

Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan-forced). Drain the chillies and blend them with the onion, garlic, chipotles, tomatoes, vinegar, cumin, oregano, cinnamon, cloves and 250ml of the stock until very smooth.

Pour the sauce into the casserole and fry, stirring, for 5 minutes until it darkens. Add the rest of the stock, the bay leaves and the beef. Bring to a simmer, cover and braise in the oven for 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until the beef falls apart.
Lift out the beef and shred it with two forks. Skim the red fat from the top of the broth into a small bowl. Taste the broth (the consommé) for salt and keep it hot.

Heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Dip a tortilla in the reserved fat, lay it in the pan, scatter with a little cheese and some beef, and fold it over. Cook for 2 minutes a side, until crisp and the cheese has melted. Repeat with the rest.
Serve the tacos with cups of hot consommé for dipping, and onion, coriander and lime on the side.
notes: The birria keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer, and tastes even better the next day.
Guajillo and ancho chillies are sold at Mexican grocers and some supermarkets. Check the tortilla label if you need these gluten-free.

image.credit: Photo: Sarah Stierch / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

recipes.title: Pão de Queijo
recipes.summary: Brazil's chewy little cheese breads, crisp outside and stretchy inside, made with tapioca starch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced) and line a tray with baking paper.

Bring the milk, oil and salt to a simmer in a small saucepan. Put the tapioca starch in a bowl, pour over the hot milk and stir hard with a wooden spoon until it forms a sticky, lumpy dough. Leave for 10 minutes to cool a little.
Beat in the egg until smooth and glossy, then the parmesan. The dough will be soft and sticky.
With oiled hands, roll the dough into 24 balls the size of a walnut and space them out on the tray.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until puffed and lightly golden. Eat warm.
notes: Brazilians use sour cassava starch (polvilho azedo), sold at Latin grocers; it gives a lighter puff. Supermarket tapioca starch works well.
Freeze the unbaked balls on a tray, then bag them. Bake from frozen, allowing 5 minutes more.

image.credit: Photo: Murilo manzini / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Gallo Pinto
recipes.summary: Costa Rica's breakfast of rice and black beans fried with onion and capsicum, with eggs and avocado.

items: 400g tin black beans, drained, with 60ml of the liquid kept
600g cooked white rice, cold from the fridge

steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and capsicum for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans and their liquid and simmer for 2 minutes, lightly crushing a few beans with the spoon.
Add the rice, soy sauce, vinegar and salt. Turn and fold for 5 to 6 minutes, until the rice is piping hot and coloured by the beans. Stir through the coriander.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs in the oil in a second pan until the whites are set.
Serve the gallo pinto with a fried egg, avocado, a spoonful of sour cream and hot sauce.
notes: In Costa Rica it's seasoned with Salsa Lizano, a tangy vegetable sauce. If you find a bottle, use 2 tbsp instead of the soy sauce and vinegar.
Use rice cooked the day before and kept in the fridge. Cooked rice shouldn't sit out at room temperature.
Runny yolks aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Fry the eggs until the yolks are firm.

image.credit: Photo: Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Ropa Vieja
recipes.summary: Cuba's shredded beef, braised slowly with capsicum, tomato and cumin, finished with green olives.

items: 1.2kg flank steak (or beef skirt), cut into 4 pieces

steps: Season the beef with the salt. Heat the oil in a large heavy saucepan or casserole over medium-high heat and brown the beef well on both sides, about 8 minutes. Set aside.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion and both capsicums and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, cumin, oregano and paprika for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for 1 minute more.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the tomatoes, stock and bay leaves, and return the beef and any juices.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low heat for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, turning the beef now and then, until it pulls apart easily.
Lift the beef onto a board and shred it along the grain with two forks. Return it to the pot with the olives and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the sauce clings. Taste for salt.
Serve over rice, scattered with parsley.
notes: Black beans and fried ripe plantain are the classic sides.
It keeps for 3 days in the fridge and freezes well.

recipes.title: Moqueca
recipes.summary: A Brazilian fish and prawn stew, simmered gently in coconut milk with capsicum, tomato and lime.

items: 600g firm white fish fillets, skinless, cut into 5cm pieces
1 brown onion, sliced into thin rings

steps: Toss the fish and prawns with the lime juice, garlic and salt. Cover and refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes, no longer, or the lime starts to firm the fish.
Heat the oil in a wide, deep frying pan or casserole over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the capsicums and cook for 5 minutes more. Stir in the paprika and chilli.
Lay the tomato slices over the vegetables, pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes.

Nestle the fish into the sauce with its marinade, cover and simmer gently for 6 minutes. Add the prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the prawns are pink and the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Taste for salt, scatter with coriander and serve with rice and lime wedges.
notes: In Bahia it's finished with a spoonful of red palm oil (dendê), sold at African and Latin grocers.
Keep the simmer gentle once the fish goes in, so the pieces stay whole.

image.credit: Photo: Bhasker Thodla / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

recipes.title: Eggs Benedict
recipes.summary: Poached eggs and ham on toasted English muffins, under a lemony, buttery hollandaise.
steps: For the hollandaise, bring a small saucepan of water to a bare simmer. In a heatproof bowl that sits snugly over the pan without touching the water, whisk the egg yolks, lemon juice and 1 tbsp water for 2 to 3 minutes, until pale, thick and leaving a trail.

Take the bowl off the heat and whisk in the warm butter a few drops at a time, then in a thin stream, until thick and glossy. Season with the salt and cayenne. If it gets too thick, whisk in a teaspoon of warm water. Keep it warm over the pan, off the heat.

Bring a wide saucepan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup. Stir the water into a slow whirlpool, slip in two eggs and poach for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Lift out onto paper towel and repeat.
Meanwhile, toast the muffins and butter them. Warm the ham briefly in a dry frying pan.
Top each muffin half with ham and a poached egg, spoon over the hollandaise and scatter with chives. Serve straight away.
notes: Soft-yolked eggs and hollandaise made with lightly cooked yolks aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. For them, poach the eggs for 5 minutes until the yolks are firm and leave off the hollandaise.
If the hollandaise splits, whisk a fresh yolk in a clean bowl over the water and slowly whisk the split sauce into it.

image.credit: Photo: Jon Mountjoy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

recipes.title: French Toast
recipes.summary: Thick slices of day-old bread soaked in cinnamon custard and fried in butter until golden.

items: 8 slices day-old white bread, about 2cm thick

steps: Heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan-forced) to keep the first batch warm.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a wide, shallow dish.
Melt a quarter of the butter in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Soak two slices of bread in the custard for 20 to 30 seconds a side, until soaked through but not falling apart.
Fry for 3 minutes a side, until deep golden and the middle feels set when pressed. Keep warm in the oven while you cook the rest, adding butter to the pan each time.
Serve with maple syrup and berries, dusted with icing sugar.
notes: Day-old bread soaks up the custard without going soggy. Fresh bread works if you dry the slices in a low oven for 10 minutes first.
Thick slices of brioche make a richer version.

recipes.title: Blackened Fish
recipes.summary: White fish crusted in a smoky Cajun spice mix and seared hard in butter, with a crunchy slaw.

items: 4 firm white fish fillets, skinless, about 180g each

steps: Mix the slaw ingredients in a bowl and set aside.
Mix the spices, salt and pepper on a plate. Pat the fish dry, brush both sides with half the melted butter and press into the spice mix to coat.
Open a window and turn on the range hood: this gets smoky. Heat a heavy frying pan (cast iron is best) over high heat for 3 minutes, then add the oil.
Cook the fish for 2 to 3 minutes a side, depending on thickness, until the crust is very dark and the fish is opaque and flakes easily. Drizzle the rest of the butter over in the last minute.
Serve with the slaw, rice and lemon wedges.
notes: Use firm fillets about 2cm thick, such as ling, barramundi or snapper. Thin fillets overcook before the crust forms.
Some ready-made Cajun seasonings are very salty. If you use one instead of the mix here, leave out the salt.

image.credit: Photo: Edsel Little / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Pot Roast
recipes.summary: Beef chuck braised slowly in red wine and stock with carrots and potatoes until it falls apart.

items: 1.5kg beef chuck roast, in one piece

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan-forced). Pat the beef dry and season all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole with a lid over medium-high heat. Brown the beef well on all sides, about 10 minutes. Set aside.
Turn the heat to medium. Cook the onions for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute and the flour for 1 minute more.

Pour in the wine and bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the stock, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves. Return the beef, bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Turn the beef, then add the carrots, celery and potatoes around it, pushing them into the liquid. Cover and cook for 1 1/2 hours more, until the beef is very tender and the vegetables are soft.
Rest the beef for 10 minutes, then pull it into thick pieces. Skim any fat from the gravy and taste for salt. Serve the beef and vegetables with plenty of gravy, scattered with parsley.
notes: Chuck has the connective tissue that melts into tenderness over a long braise. Leaner cuts like topside go dry.
Leftovers make great sandwiches the next day.

image.credit: Photo: Mark Miller / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Welsh Rarebit
recipes.summary: A savoury cheddar, ale and mustard sauce spread thickly on toast and grilled until bubbling.
steps: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beer until smooth, then the mustard and Worcestershire. Simmer for 2 minutes until thick.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cheese until melted, then the egg yolk and pepper. Leave to cool for 5 minutes, until it's a thick paste.
Heat the grill to high. Toast the bread on both sides under the grill.
Spread the cheese mixture thickly over the toast, right to the edges. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes, until bubbling and browned in patches. Serve hot with salad leaves.
notes: Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies, so this isn't vegetarian. Some brands make an anchovy-free version.
The cheese mixture keeps for 3 days in the fridge, ready for quick lunches.

image.credit: Photo: Jeremy Keith / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

recipes.title: Cornish Pasties
recipes.summary: Short pastry crimped around raw beef, potato, swede and onion, baked so the filling steams in its own juices.

items: 450g beef skirt steak, cut into 1cm pieces

steps: For the pastry, mix the flour and salt in a bowl and rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Add the water and bring together into a dough without kneading much. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced) and line a large tray with baking paper.
Cut the pastry into four pieces and roll each out on a floured bench to a circle about 22cm across and 4mm thick, using a plate as a guide.
Layer a quarter of the potato, swede, onion and beef across the middle of each circle, seasoning each layer with salt and plenty of pepper. Top with a piece of butter.

Brush the edge with egg, bring the pastry up over the filling and press the edges together along the top. Crimp the seam by folding it over itself in small pleats. Cut a small steam hole in each side and brush all over with egg.

Bake for 20 minutes, then turn the oven down to 170°C (150°C fan-forced) and bake for 30 minutes more, until deep golden and a skewer slides easily through the vegetables. Rest for 10 minutes before eating.
notes: Everything goes in raw: the beef and vegetables cook in the steam sealed inside the pastry, so cut them small and thin.
Skirt is the traditional cut. Chuck steak works too, cut finely.

image.credit: Photo: David Johnson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

recipes.title: Fish Pie
recipes.summary: White fish, salmon, smoked salmon and prawns in a creamy parsley sauce under a buttery mash crust.

items: 400g firm white fish fillets, skinless, cut into 3cm pieces
250g salmon fillet, skinless, cut into 3cm pieces

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain well, mash with the butter, milk and salt, and set aside.
Meanwhile, warm the milk with the bay leaf and onion in a saucepan until steaming. Turn off the heat and leave for 10 minutes, then discard the bay leaf and onion.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced). Melt the butter in a clean saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring, until thick. Stir in the mustard, lemon juice and salt, and take off the heat.
Spread the raw fish, salmon, smoked salmon, prawns and peas in a 2.5L baking dish. Stir the parsley through the sauce and pour it over evenly.
Spoon the mash over the top, starting at the edges to seal in the filling, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheese.

Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Check a piece of fish in the middle: it should be opaque and flake easily. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Fish pie packs from the supermarket seafood counter make this quicker; use 1kg in total.
Assemble up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Bake from cold for 45 minutes.

recipes.title: Scotch Eggs
recipes.summary: Jammy-yolked eggs wrapped in herby sausage meat, crumbed and fried until crisp.
steps: Lower the 6 eggs into a saucepan of boiling water and boil for 6 1/2 minutes. Move straight into iced water for 10 minutes, then peel carefully.

Mix the sausage mince with the sage, pepper and nutmeg and divide into six. Flatten each portion into a thin patty on a piece of baking paper, sit an egg in the middle and wrap the meat around it, pinching to seal with no gaps.
Roll each in flour, then the beaten egg, then the panko, pressing it on. Chill for 15 minutes.

Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced). Heat the oil in a deep, heavy saucepan to 160°C, no more than a third full. Fry the eggs two or three at a time for 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until deep golden. Drain on paper towel.

Put them on a tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the sausage meat is cooked through (75°C when a thermometer is pushed into the meat). Rest for 5 minutes, then halve and serve warm or cold with mustard.
notes: Runny yolks aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Boil the eggs for 9 minutes for firm yolks.
Never leave hot oil unattended. Let it cool completely before you move or strain it.
Sausage mince is sold at the meat counter. Or squeeze good pork sausages out of their skins.

image.credit: Photo: Unhindered by Talent / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Käsespätzle
recipes.summary: Soft homemade egg noodles layered with melting Gruyère and emmental under sweet fried onions.
steps: Beat the flour, eggs, milk, salt and nutmeg with a wooden spoon for 3 to 4 minutes, until the batter is thick, smooth and starts to bubble. Rest for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the onions for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and soft. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced) and butter a baking dish.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Press a third of the batter through a spätzle maker or a colander with large holes into the water. When the spätzle float, after about 1 minute, lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Layer the hot spätzle in the dish with the cheeses and pepper, finishing with cheese. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Top with the onions and bake for 10 minutes, until the cheese has melted through. Scatter with chives and serve with a green salad.
notes: If the batter won't drip through the holes, add a splash more milk. If it runs straight through, beat in a little more flour.
The cheeses are made with animal rennet, which some vegetarians avoid.

recipes.title: Kaiserschmarrn
recipes.summary: Austria's fluffy torn pancake with rum-soaked raisins, caramelised in the pan and dusted with icing sugar.
steps: Soak the raisins in the rum (or warm water) for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and vanilla, then whisk in the milk and flour until smooth. In a clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks, then fold them gently into the batter.

Melt half the butter in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Pour in the batter and scatter over the drained raisins. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the underside is golden and the top is starting to set.
Cut the pancake into quarters and flip each one. Cook for 3 minutes more, then tear into bite-sized pieces with two forks.
Add the rest of the butter and the extra sugar and toss for 2 minutes, until the edges caramelise and the pieces are cooked through. Dust with icing sugar and serve with apple sauce.
notes: It's meant to look rough: the torn pieces catch the caramel.
Stewed plums are the traditional partner if you have them.

recipes.title: Bigos
recipes.summary: Poland's hunter's stew of sauerkraut, cabbage, pork, kransky and porcini, slow-cooked until mellow.
steps: Soak the porcini in the boiling water for 15 minutes. Lift them out, chop them and keep the soaking liquid, leaving any grit behind in the bowl.

In a large heavy saucepan over medium heat, fry the bacon for 5 minutes until the fat runs. Add the pork and brown for 8 minutes. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the sauerkraut, cabbage, apple, porcini and their liquid, wine, stock, bay leaves, allspice, caraway and pepper. Stir well and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Add the kransky and cook uncovered for 30 minutes more, until the pork is very tender and the stew is thick. Taste for salt; the sauerkraut and bacon may be enough. Serve with rye bread.
notes: Bigos is better the next day and better still the day after. It keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.
A handful of chopped prunes added with the cabbage is traditional and adds a gentle sweetness.

image.credit: Photo: Dr. Bernd Gross / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

recipes.title: Lecsó
recipes.summary: Hungary's summer stew of yellow capsicum, tomato and onion with sweet paprika, with eggs stirred through.
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wide saucepan over medium heat. If using the kransky, fry it for 3 minutes until browned and lift it out.
Cook the onions for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the capsicums and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until softened.

Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika (it burns easily), then return to the heat and add the tomatoes, salt and sugar. Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until the tomatoes have collapsed into a thick sauce. Return the kransky, if using.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set in soft curds.
Serve straight away with crusty bread.
notes: Long, pale Hungarian wax peppers are traditional. Look for them at greengrocers in late summer.
Without the eggs, lecsó is also a great sauce for sausages or rice.

recipes.title: Pytt i Panna
recipes.summary: A Swedish hash of crisp diced potato, ham, kransky and onion, topped with fried eggs and pickled beetroot.
steps: Pat the potatoes dry with a tea towel. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the potatoes for 18 to 20 minutes, turning every few minutes, until golden, crisp and tender. Tip into a bowl.
Turn the heat to medium. Add half the butter and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the ham and kransky and fry for 5 minutes until browned.
Return the potatoes with the rest of the butter, season with the salt and pepper and toss for 2 minutes until hot through. Stir in the parsley.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs in the rest of the oil in a second pan until the whites are set.
Divide the hash between plates and top each with a fried egg, with pickled beetroot on the side.
notes: It's the Swedish way of using up a roast: swap the ham for leftover roast beef or pork.
Runny yolks aren't recommended for pregnant people, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Fry the eggs until the yolks are firm.

recipes.title: Toast Skagen
recipes.summary: Sweden's classic prawn toast: cold prawns in a dill and lemon dressing, piled on butter-fried bread.

items: 400g cooked prawns, peeled and roughly chopped

steps: Mix the mayonnaise, crème fraîche, mustard, dill, chives and lemon juice. Fold in the prawns and season with white pepper and salt. Keep in the fridge until needed.
Cut the crusts off the bread and halve each slice diagonally. Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the bread for 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden.
Pile the prawn mixture onto the warm toast and top each with a dill sprig. Serve straight away with lemon wedges.
notes: Keep the prawns cold until the last minute, and don't leave the finished toasts out for more than 2 hours.
A spoonful of salmon roe on top is the traditional finish.

recipes.title: Jansson's Temptation
recipes.summary: A Swedish gratin of potato matchsticks, sweet onion and anchovies baked in cream until golden.

items: 1kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
60g anchovy fillets, drained and chopped, oil kept

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced) and butter a 2L baking dish with a little of the butter.
Melt half the remaining butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and pale gold.
Spread a third of the potatoes in the dish, then half the onions and half the anchovies. Repeat, finishing with a layer of potato. Season with the pepper; the anchovies bring enough salt.
Warm the cream, milk and 1 tbsp of the anchovy oil and pour it over. Scatter with the breadcrumbs and dot with the rest of the butter.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the top is golden, the cream has thickened and a knife slides easily through the potatoes. Rest for 10 minutes and serve with a green salad.
notes: Swedish 'ansjovis' are sprats in a sweet spiced brine, sold at IKEA food markets. If you find them, use a 125g tin and its brine instead of the anchovies.
It's a Christmas table classic in Sweden, and good alongside roast meats.

image.credit: Photo: Anders Jonsson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

recipes.title: Aussie Meat Pies
recipes.summary: Individual pies of rich beef mince gravy in flaky puff pastry, with tomato sauce on top.

items: 4 sheets frozen puff pastry, just thawed

steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.

Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute. Add the tomato sauce, Worcestershire, stock, salt and pepper. Simmer gently, stirring now and then, for 25 minutes, until thick enough to hold its shape. Spread on a tray to cool for 20 minutes, then refrigerate until cold.
Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan-forced) with a tray inside. Grease a 6-hole Texas muffin tin (or six 10cm pie tins).
Cut six 14cm circles from the pastry for the bases and six 10cm circles for the lids, re-chilling the pastry if it goes soft. Press the bases into the tin and fill with the cold filling.
Brush the pastry edges with egg, put the lids on and press to seal. Brush the tops with egg and cut a small slit in each.

Set the tin on the hot tray and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until puffed and deep golden and the filling is piping hot (75°C in the centre). Rest for 5 minutes, then lift out and serve with tomato sauce.
notes: Cold filling stops the pastry going soggy. Make it the day before if you like; cover and refrigerate once cooled.
Cooked pies freeze well. Reheat from frozen at 180°C (160°C fan-forced) for 25 minutes, until piping hot.

image.credit: Photo: Philip Mallis / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

recipes.title: Zucchini Slice
recipes.summary: The lunchbox classic: grated zucchini, bacon and cheese baked into an easy, sliceable bake.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced). Grease and line a 20 x 30cm slice tin with baking paper.
Squeeze the grated zucchini lightly in your hands to get rid of some of the water.
In a large bowl, mix the zucchini, onion, bacon, cheese and flour.
Whisk the eggs, oil, salt and pepper, pour into the bowl with the parsley and mix well. Spread evenly in the tin.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and firm in the middle when pressed. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Serve warm or cold.
notes: For a vegetarian slice, leave out the bacon and add a grated carrot and a handful of corn kernels.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge and freezes well in portions.

recipes.title: Sang Choy Bow
recipes.summary: Quick stir-fried pork mince with water chestnuts and oyster sauce, eaten in cool iceberg lettuce cups.

items: 225g tin water chestnuts, drained and chopped
1 iceberg lettuce, leaves separated into cups

steps: Trim the lettuce cups with scissors into neat bowls and keep them in iced water while you cook, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the pork and stir-fry for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through with no pink left.
Add the carrot and water chestnuts and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and sesame oil and toss for 1 minute.
Take off the heat and toss through the bean sprouts and most of the spring onion.
Spoon the filling into lettuce cups at the table, topped with fried shallots, chilli, the rest of the spring onion and a little hoisin.
notes: Chicken mince works just as well.
Water chestnuts are what give it the crunch, so don't skip them.

recipes.title: Ricotta Hotcakes
recipes.summary: Tall, soft hotcakes made light with ricotta and whipped egg whites, served with maple syrup and berries.
steps: Mix the ricotta, milk, egg yolks and sugar in a bowl. Sift in the flour and baking powder and stir until just combined.
In a clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks. Fold them through the batter in two batches, keeping as much air as you can.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat and brush with a little butter. Drop in 1/4 cup of batter per hotcake, leaving room to spread.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden underneath and set around the edges. Flip carefully and cook for 2 minutes more, until golden and springy in the middle. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.
Serve stacked, with maple syrup and berries, dusted with icing sugar.
notes: Use fresh ricotta from the deli counter if you can. Tub ricotta is wetter; drain it in a sieve for 15 minutes first.
Sliced banana and a slice of honey butter is the cafe way to serve them.

image.credit: Photo: Sarah Stierch / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

recipes.title: Crispy-Skin Barramundi with Greens
recipes.summary: Pan-fried barramundi with shatteringly crisp skin, spring greens, baby potatoes and a caper herb dressing.
steps: Mix the dressing ingredients and set aside.

Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender. Add the broccolini, sugar snaps and asparagus for the last 2 minutes, then drain. Toss the greens and potatoes with the olive oil and garlic and keep warm.
Meanwhile, pat the fish skin very dry with paper towel and score it two or three times. Season both sides with the salt.

Heat the neutral oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Lay the fillets in skin side down and press them flat with a spatula for the first 30 seconds so the skin doesn't curl. Cook without moving for 5 to 6 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the flesh is opaque most of the way up.
Flip, add the butter and cook for 1 minute more, until the fish is just opaque in the middle and flakes easily.
Serve the fish skin side up on the potatoes and greens, with the dressing spooned around (not on the skin, which keeps it crisp).
notes: Dry skin is the whole trick. If you have time, leave the fillets uncovered on a plate in the fridge for an hour first.
Snapper or salmon fillets work the same way.
